classes.C: cells and microbes (natural or wild-type strains; experimental evolution allowed; engineered strains excluded)
classes.A: non-human animals in wild or wild-caught populations (domesticated, captive-bred and laboratory-model lines excluded)
classes.F: firms and markets (competitive markets with entry and exit; the design variable not set by regulation or mandate)

D1.statement: When the tracked world drifts faster (higher volatility or drift rate), reading, sampling, updating or adjustment rate rises.
D1.source: CT12 (read rate proportional to (w q / c)^(1/alpha)); CT10; CT41/CL19 (inaction band narrows in time as drift rises)
D1.conditions: ruin slack; read price fixed; drift below the G3 (Lemma B1) collapse edge where a bounded fallback exists
D1.known_exception: Lemma B1 (G3): with a bounded fallback, effort rises then collapses at high drift. A hump or fall is scored as 0 or -1, never rescued.

D2.statement: When the stake of being wrong rises (e.g. predation risk), spending on judgment (vigilance, monitoring) rises.
D2.conditions: ruin slack (PF2 / CT33: may flip when ruin binds; a study is ruin-binding only if it manipulated or documented starvation or energetic stress)

D3.statement: When the world stops presenting the signal or the stake goes to zero (relaxed selection), the costly tracking/sensing trait shrinks or is lost.
D3.source: CT4 (the first bit must pay); CT9/CT11 (hold vs fade); freeze limit, theory/FREEZE_PROCESS_2026-11-21.md section 2 (PR #137)
D3.conditions: trait has positive upkeep (kappa or h > 0); enough generations

rivals.Rdrift neutral mutation accumulation: same sign (LOW DISCRIMINATION; drift also predicts loss)

D4.statement: A reserve or buffer grows with the size of the shocks it must absorb (and their persistence).
D4.source: CT25 (buffer grows as shock x tau^H); CT22 (B_min)
D4.conditions: none beyond the model class; binding ruin does not flip this sign

D5.statement: Fast-changing information is handled locally and slow-changing information is shared: when the world changes faster, decision rights or information use shift from shared/central/social to local/individual.
D5.source: CT35 with the OU closed form X_S = nu*pi*exp(-2 l/tau)*X_L (THEORY Appendix B.11, line 488); CORE section 5 row CT14...CT34
D5.conditions: the shared level adds latency l > 0; equal read quality

cells.query: experimental evolution fluctuating environment phenotypic plasticity bacteria
cells.plus: lines evolved or populations living under fluctuating conditions show more regulation, sensing, plasticity, switching or faster response than constant-environment lines

cells.query: experimental evolution relaxed selection loss of unused function bacteria
cells.plus: an unused sensing, regulatory, motility or catabolic function declines or is lost when it is not needed

cells.query: storage polymer accumulation fluctuating nutrient supply bacteria
cells.plus: more storage (glycogen, PHA/PHB, polyphosphate, trehalose, lipid) under fluctuating or intermittent supply than under constant supply

cells.query: sampling behaviour environmental variability foraging animals
cells.plus: more sampling, exploration, information gathering or faster updating in more variable or faster-changing environments
vigilance higher when predation risk is higher

cells.query: loss of antipredator behaviour relaxed predation island
cells.plus: antipredator behaviour or predator recognition reduced in populations with relaxed or absent predation
larger fat or energy reserves (or more hoarding) when food supply is more unpredictable

cells.query: social learning versus individual learning environmental change animals
cells.plus: less reliance on social information (more individual learning) when the environment changes faster
firms change prices more often when inflation or cost volatility is higher

cells.query: corporate cash holdings cash flow volatility
cells.plus: firms with more volatile cash flows (or higher cash-flow risk) hold more cash
more decentralization (decision rights delegated to local units) under higher environmental uncertainty or volatility

codes.0: abstract reports no effect, a mixed result, or a non-monotone (hump) relation

scoring.primary_per_class: k = count(+1); n = all included; one-sided exact binomial P(X >= k | n, 0.5)
scoring.sign_test_vs_R0: among nonzero codes, one-sided exact binomial P(X >= count(+1) | n_nonzero, 0.5)
scoring.FAIL: pooled rate <= 0.60, or two or more classes fail
scoring.PASS: two or more classes support and no FAIL condition
scoring.coding_reliability_gate: a blind recode of 20 included systems (random, seed 20261121) by the independent reviewer; agreement < 0.80 labels the verdict UNRELIABLE CODING
